status: Proposed story and design work; owner review required before canon or rules change

books.title: Altered Carbon
books.focus: IVXX: identity when the signal home is compromised
books.question: When the records disagree, what makes a person continuous—and who gets to decide?
books.task: Draft an original IVXX scene in which a surviving memory and a damaged signal disagree. Separate what IVXX observes, what she infers and the choice she can still make.
books.review: Keep the compromised-signal connection from the primer. Review the new scene against the owning story source; do not import the novel’s characters, setting or plot.

books.title: Ancillary Justice
books.question: What changes when an entity capable of force chooses restraint instead?
books.task: Draft a conversation between conflicting perspectives within a distributed system. Give restraint a visible cost and consequence; compare it with Rebirth’s established design tension.
books.review: The conversation is a proposal, not a new canonical identity or ability. Check consistency with the project’s existing characters and limits.

books.title: Annihilation
books.question: What can a character observe at a boundary without being able to explain it?
books.task: Write two original accounts of the same encounter near a Veiled boundary. Mark shared observations, incompatible interpretations and the decision left uncertain.
books.review: Use uncertainty to shape the scene. Preserve the canonical four-player Veiling lifecycle; atmosphere is not permission to change a rule.

books.title: The Left Hand of Darkness
books.question: What does a shared story allow a community to do, and whose experience does it leave out?
books.task: Propose two tellings of one original in-world event. Show how each telling changes trust, obligations or an available choice rather than serving as decorative lore.
books.review: Record any new event or community as proposed. Owner review determines whether it belongs in this project’s continuity.

books.title: Children of Time
books.focus: Asymmetric intelligence and forms of power
books.question: Can two sides understand the same problem while recognizing different possible solutions?
books.task: Draft an original encounter from two perspectives with different constraints. Connect the contrast to Veiled Dominion’s existing asymmetry without treating one side as simply less intelligent.
books.review: Check that the encounter follows current faction capabilities. New abilities, species or historical events remain proposals.

books.title: Rules of Play
books.focus: Win conditions, feedback loops and asymmetric balance
books.question: What behavior does a rule reward, and does that behavior tell the story we intend?
books.task: Choose one existing playtest decision. Map the player action, rule, feedback and narrative interpretation; write a short scene or debrief showing the resulting consequence.
books.review: Cite the current rule version and observed playtest evidence. Separate a proposed adjustment from the rule actually implemented.

books.title: The Art of Game Design
books.focus: Martyr’s Boon: voluntary cost and consequence
books.question: Does the player understand the sacrifice, its benefit and the alternatives before choosing?
books.task: Storyboard an original Martyr’s Boon decision: establish the situation, present the existing legal options, show informed choice and follow through on its consequence.
books.review: Use the current canonical Boon rule rather than inventing a new reward. Test clarity and agency before proposing balance changes.
